DnsDetail.description:
What one DNS question found.

`resolver` is `system` (the node's own resolvers; their addresses are never reported) or the
public resolver that was asked. A response code other than NOERROR (`NXDOMAIN` is the usual
one) is still an answer. `redacted` counts answers from the node's own resolver that were
private addresses: they are left out, so a result never discloses someone's internal DNS.
DnsDetail.title: DnsDetail

GeoIpOut.description:
What a GeoIP database says about the address, checked against the measurements.

It never changes the estimate. `ruled_out` means a node measured the address too close for the
database's place to be right; `consistent` only means no measurement contradicts it.

distance_to_estimate_km.description: From the place the database names to the likely place
distance_to_estimate_km.title: Distance To Estimate Km

GeoIpOut.title: GeoIpOut

HopDetail.description:
One traceroute hop: the router that answered at this TTL.

`ip` is only ever a public address. A router inside the node operator's own network (or any
other non-public address) is reported as `private` with no address, so a result never
discloses the layout of someone's LAN.

A trace of one round sends three probes to a hop. When it is repeated (`count` above one),
`sent` says how many probes went to this hop and `rtts_us` has one entry for each that was
answered, so the hop's loss is `1 - len(rtts_us) / sent`.
HopDetail.title: HopDetail

HopPlaceOut.description:
What a GeoIP database says about one router on a path. Routers are often registered at the
owner's headquarters, so the place is a hint to be checked against the round-trip time, never a
fact.

place.description: City, or the country if no city is known
place.title: Place

HopPlaceOut.title: HopPlaceOut

HttpDetail.description:
What one HTTP request found. Times are microseconds, measured on the node.

`total_us` covers the whole exchange, redirects included. The phases (`dns_us`, `connect_us`,
`tls_us`, `ttfb_us`) and `tls` belong to the final request, whose address is `final_host`.
HttpDetail.title: HttpDetail

TlsDetail.description:
What one certificate check found: a TLS handshake with no request after it. Times are
microseconds, measured on the node.

`tls` is the same record an HTTP check carries (version, cipher, subject, issuer, validity, whether
this node trusts the certificate and why not). `names` are the names the certificate is valid for
and `chain` is how many certificates the server sent. A certificate that is not trusted still
comes with all of it: the point of the check is to see what is wrong.
TlsDetail.title: TlsDetail

post.description:
Ask verified official nodes to ping the node's address and check its declared place against the answers.

It stores what it found (`location_audit`) and changes nothing else: whether to mark the place verified
is the administrator's decision. It waits for the measurement (up to 30 s).
